canvas.$description: The app background, behind every surface. Not for cards, panels or menus: use color.bg.surface, raised or overlay.

surface.$description: Cards, panels, table bodies and inputs that sit on the canvas. Not for floating layers: use color.bg.raised (popovers, dropdowns) or color.bg.overlay (dialogs).

raised.$description: Layers that float above a surface: popovers, dropdown menus, tooltips. Not for content that scrolls with the page: use color.bg.surface.

overlay.$description: The top layer: dialogs, drawers, command palettes. Not for the dimmed backdrop behind a dialog, and not for ordinary cards.

inset.$description: Recessed areas inside a surface: wells, code blocks, secondary buttons, table headers. Not a hover state: use color.interactive.hover.

scrim.$description: The translucent backdrop behind a modal dialog, a drawer or a sheet. Not a surface and not a hover wash: nothing is read on it. Use color.bg.overlay for the dialog itself.

default.$description: Body text, headings and icons that carry meaning. Not for text on a solid accent background (use color.fg.on-accent) or a solid status background (use that status's solid-fg).

muted.$description: Secondary text: labels, descriptions, captions, inactive tabs. Not for disabled content (use color.fg.disabled) and not for body text.

subtle.$description: Tertiary text: placeholders, hints, timestamps, decorative icons. Not for anything the user must read to complete a task: use color.fg.muted or default.

disabled.$description: Text and icons of disabled controls. Never for readable content: it is below text contrast on purpose (WCAG exempts disabled controls).

link.$description: Hyperlinks and link-styled buttons in running text. Not for emphasis and not on a solid accent background.

on-accent.$description: Text and icons on color.accent.bg and its hover and pressed colours. Not on a solid status background (use that status's solid-fg, which can differ) and not on neutral backgrounds (use color.fg.default).

muted.$description: The faintest separator: hairlines inside a dense list or between rows of a table. Not the outline of a card or a control: use color.border.default or color.border.strong.

default.$description: Separators and the outline of cards, panels and table cells. Not the only cue that identifies a control (it is below 3:1): use color.border.strong.

strong.$description: The outline that identifies a control: inputs, checkboxes, outlined buttons (at least 3:1). Not for separators between content: use color.border.default.

focus.$description: The border of a focused input, where the ring is drawn as the border itself. Not the outline drawn around a focused element: use ring.color with ring.width.

ring.$description: The focus ring of any focusable element. Not a decorative border and not a selection colour: use color.interactive.selected.

fg.$description: Text and icons on color.accent.bg and its hover and pressed colours (the same colour as color.fg.on-accent). Not on color.accent.subtle-bg: use color.accent.subtle-fg.

bg.$description: The filled background of the primary action and of checked controls. Not for large areas, and not more than one primary action per view.

bg-hover.$description: color.accent.bg while hovered. Not a resting colour.

bg-active.$description: color.accent.bg while pressed. Not a resting colour.

subtle-bg.$description: A tinted background for accent badges, tags and highlighted callouts. Not for the selected row or item: use color.interactive.selected.

subtle-fg.$description: Text and icons on color.accent.subtle-bg. Not on color.accent.bg: use color.accent.fg.

hover.$description: A translucent wash over any background for hovered rows, menu items and ghost buttons. Not for filled controls: use the role's own hover token (color.accent.bg-hover).

active.$description: The same wash while pressed. Not for a persistent selected state: use color.interactive.selected.

selected.$description: A translucent accent wash for the selected row, item or tab. Not for hover, and not for text selection inside an editor.

selected-hover.$description: The selected wash while the pointer is over the selected row, item or tab. Not for an unselected item: use color.interactive.hover.

drag.$description: A translucent wash, in the blue ramp so it stays apart from selection, for an item being dragged and for the drop target it is over. Not for selection or hover.

instant.$description: 0 ms, for changes that must not animate (reduced motion, drag following the pointer). Primitive: reference it through a role, never from a component. Not above 240 ms for interface feedback, and not when the user prefers reduced motion: switch to motion.duration.instant.

fast.$description: 100 ms, for hover and focus feedback, small toggles. Primitive: reference it through a role, never from a component. Not above 240 ms for interface feedback, and not when the user prefers reduced motion: switch to motion.duration.instant.

base.$description: 160 ms, for menus, popovers, tooltips and most transitions. Primitive: reference it through a role, never from a component. Not above 240 ms for interface feedback, and not when the user prefers reduced motion: switch to motion.duration.instant.

slow.$description: 240 ms, for dialogs, drawers and layout changes. Primitive: reference it through a role, never from a component. Not above 240 ms for interface feedback, and not when the user prefers reduced motion: switch to motion.duration.instant.

standard.$description: The standard curve, for elements that move or change between two resting states. Not linear easing for movement, and not a custom curve: pick one of the four so the interface moves alike.

enter.$description: The enter curve, for elements that appear: they start fast and settle. Not linear easing for movement, and not a custom curve: pick one of the four so the interface moves alike.

exit.$description: The exit curve, for elements that leave: they start slowly and speed up. Not linear easing for movement, and not a custom curve: pick one of the four so the interface moves alike.

emphasized.$description: The emphasized curve, for large movements that should draw the eye: drawers, dialogs. Not linear easing for movement, and not a custom curve: pick one of the four so the interface moves alike.

none.$description: Square corners: table cells, full-bleed panels, dividers. Not for controls and containers, which follow the radius seed: use radius.md or radius.lg.

xs.$description: The smallest rounding: focus outlines on inline text, code chips, scrollbar thumbs. Not for controls: use radius.sm or radius.md.

sm.$description: Small elements: checkboxes, tags, extra-small controls. Not for standard controls: use radius.md.

md.$description: Standard controls: buttons, inputs, menu items. Not for containers: use radius.lg.

lg.$description: Containers: cards, popovers, dialogs. Not for controls inside those containers: use radius.md.

xl.$description: Large containers: sheets, drawers, big cards. Not for controls and not for small containers: use radius.md or radius.lg.

full.$description: Pills and circles: avatars, switches, badges, round icon buttons. Not for rectangles that happen to be small: use radius.sm.
